params.body:
## What

Two things on Inzichten > Werking.

### 1. The top of the tab is one compact unit

The tab spent a full row on one text action and a timestamp, then a full-width card of three lines for one sentence. The verdict is now the first thing on the tab; when it was measured and "Nu verversen" stand as a quiet note on the verdict's own line, at the right end; what wants attention stands close under the verdict. With nothing wrong the surface is one line high.

Height from the top of the tab to the card of checks:

| | 1440 before | 1440 after | 390 before | 390 after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nothing wrong | 162 px | 74 px | 174 px | 98 px |
| one item | 200 px | 104 px | 235 px | 151 px |
| three items | 253 px | 157 px | 310 px | 226 px |

Part of the old height was an accident: the `@if` around the `after` slot left Livewire's block markers in the default slot, the head took them for figures and drew an empty figures row with its gap. The condition now stands inside the slot.

The pattern (R P2-10.46) gains a form for a tab that has nothing to filter: no filter line, and the note that line would have held goes to the answer surface (`x-insights.head` with a `note` slot, class `ins-head--noted`). `EveryInsightsTabStandsOnOnePatternTest` now names the tabs without a filter line (Werking only) and checks both forms; `docs/design-system.md` and the components README describe it. The other tabs render the same head as before (same class, same padding, measured on Momentum, Klanten en omzet, Gebruik and Kaart).

The rest of the tab, within the same rules (text roles, tokens, no new colour, no `!important`):

- From 640 px up the states stand in one column right beside the subjects instead of at the far edge of a 1390 px card, and a fold opens under the state it explains (capped in width). On a phone the lines are as they were.
- A line with nothing behind it is a plain line, not a fold that opens on nothing or on a repeat of its own state: no call to a partner, no report.
- The partner line said "no call to a partner in 7 days" whenever nothing was refused, also when there were calls. It now says how many calls and that nothing was refused.
- The note says the hour only: the facts are at most a minute old.

### 2. The clock says what it knows

With no heartbeat in the cache the screen printed "laatste teken ? geleden". The heartbeat now has four states (`Operations::heartbeat`), each said in words in nl, fr, en and de:

- `alive`: a beat of at most five minutes old.
- `stale`: a beat that is too old. Red, with its age ("laatste teken 12 min geleden"). Never excused by a fresh release: the cache survived the deploy, so the scheduler had its minutes.
- `silent`: no beat was ever kept. Red, and the line says what that usually means (the cache was emptied and the scheduler has not come round since, or the scheduler does not run). The fold names the next step.
- `waiting`: no beat yet and the release landed less than five minutes ago. Calm, not in the verdict: "wacht op het eerste teken na de uitrol".

**What empties the key.** `elixir:scheduler` is written with `Cache::forever` by `elixir:beat` and by every starting scheduled task, in the default cache store (the file store on the servers). `php artisan optimize` in `deploy/build.sh` does not touch it. What does: `cache:clear`, which eight migrations call to make the menu read again, `optimize:clear`, and a manual `cache:clear` (CUTOVER.md names one). So a deploy that carries such a migration empties the key, and until the scheduler's next minute there is no beat; the screen then showed a dead clock, for up to a minute plus the minute the screen itself is cached.

**The grace.** Tied to the build stamp of the checkout (`App\Elixir\BuildStamp`, the same one `/.well-known/build.json` publishes). That stamp is the start of the deploy; composer, npm and the build come between it and the migration, so the grace is five minutes (`Operations::RELEASE_GRACE`), the same tolerance an old beat already gets, and not one. No readable stamp means no grace. A scheduler that is really dead is red at once without a release, and at most five minutes after one.

## Tests

`OperationsScreenTest` (all `@rule P3-14.4`, two also `P3-14.2`): never seen and no fresh release is the alarm and prints no age; no beat right after a release is waiting and not in the verdict; the grace ends at five minutes and is absent without a checkout; a beat that is too old says how old and no release excuses it; every language says each state. The test builds its own checkout with a dated `HEAD` (config `elixir.release_root`), so the outcome does not depend on how long ago CI checked out.

`EveryInsightsTabStandsOnOnePatternTest`: the no-filter form, and no empty figures row on Werking.

Rules updated: R P3-14.2, R P3-14.4, R P3-14.11, R P2-10.46.

## Not checked

- Which of the two happened on production when the screen showed the question mark (a deploy that emptied the cache, or a scheduler that does not beat): this PR was built without access to production. After the merge the line itself says which: "wacht op het eerste teken" turning into "klopt" within a minute is the first, "gaf nog geen teken" that stays is the second.
- That a release on the server carries a `.git` whose `HEAD` is dated at the deploy. If it does not, there is no grace and the behaviour is the old alarm, with honest words.
- `/api/elixir` reports the same missing key to Elixir as "no scheduler"; that endpoint is unchanged.
- The Koppelingen fold (only shown to an administrator with the `vwe` right) was not in the local screenshots; its panel keeps the full width of the card.
params.title: Werking: the verdict first on one compact surface, and a clock that says what it knows
